text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Macedonia receives support for membership in the U.N. Security Council from the Chinese, Turkish and Croat foreign ministers in New York where the Macedonian delegation, headed by President Gligorov, is attending the General Assembly session.
- Police discover over 2,000 archeological objects illegally excavated in eastern Macedonia estimated to be worth 5 million German marks, and arrest three persons.
- Additional taxes to be imposed on cooking oil imports with the aim of protecting domestic production.
- Electricity prices to go up by 10 percent starting from October 1.
- Macedonia has been admitted as a full member of the Mediterranean Association within the Interparliamentarian Union.
- Over 300 workers in Protex garment factory in Probistip continue their strike.
- Justice minister Vlado Popovski tells news conference that 1,920 members of municipal councils are to be elected at forthcoming elections.
- The Health ministry told a news conference that a law on the production and abuse of narcotics had to be adopted immediately.
- U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali expected to visit Macedonia by the end of January 1997.
